newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity prices mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity prices mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were mixed at midday Friday in thin trade that was marked by a lack of news, industry sources said.
"It's basically unchanged, things have quieted down from the big volume we saw yesterday," said a New York futures trader.

As of 1215 EDT, NYMEX July California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were up 16 cents at the day's high of $18.25 following trade as low as $17.25 per megawatt hour (MWh), while August was down two cents at the day's high of $22.40 after exchange as low as $21.75 per MWh.
July Palo Verde (PV) was up 13 cents at the day's high of $28.30 after reaching as low as $27.70, while August was up 19 cents at the day's high of $31.30 after reaching as low as $31.15 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1130 EDT an estimated total of 84 COB and 32 PV contracts had traded.
As of 1215 EDT, July NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 0.7 cents at $2.17 per million British thermal units.
In the West, the 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 1 on the coast of central California and 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3 near Phoenix, Arizona, both reached full power early Friday after recent outages.
A 550 MW unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired plant in Wyoming was expected to restart Sunday after being shut for planned maintenance earlier this week, industry sources said.

Meterologists said temperatures in the West would average near to slightly below normal through the weekend. In a six to 10 day outlook, readings across the region were forecast to run at to above seasonal levels.
